mnemonic.meaning: Your lazy self (我 self, 慢 lazy) begs to quit the marathon at mile 20. You grit your teeth and keep putting up with the pain. That's endurance.
mnemonic.reading: "GAH, MAN!" (がまん) you groan at every step, but you keep enduring.

examples.ja: 痛かったけど、最後まで我慢した。
examples.en: It hurt, but I put up with it until the end.

items.note: 我慢する means to endure or hold back. Don't mix it up with 自慢 (じまん), bragging.

mnemonic.meaning: Every season (節) you make a promise (約) to cut down on spending: no taxis, no coffee shop. That's saving money, economizing.
mnemonic.reading: You SET YOUR YAK (せつやく) loose in the field instead of buying lawnmower fuel. Saving money!

examples.ja: 電気代を節約するために、エアコンを消した。
examples.en: I turned off the air conditioner to save on electricity.

items.note: 節約 = use less. 貯金 = put money aside.

mnemonic.meaning: 冷 is cold. Breathe on hot food to make it cold: you let it cool.
mnemonic.reading: Uncle SAM'S SOUP (さます) is scalding, so he blows on it and lets it cool. (冷める さめる = it cools by itself.)

examples.ja: 熱いお茶を冷ますために、しばらく置いておく。
examples.en: I leave the hot tea for a while to let it cool.

items.note: 冷ます and 覚ます (wake someone up) are both さます. The other reading of 冷, ひ, is used in 冷やす.

mnemonic.meaning: A surgeon's hands (手) need the finest technique (術). Hand technique on the operating table: surgery.
mnemonic.reading: The surgeon's ninja move: SHOE-JUTSU (しゅじゅつ). He sews you up so fast you never see it. Surgery done.

examples.ja: 父は来週、胃の手術を受ける。
examples.en: My father is having stomach surgery next week.

items.note: 手術を受ける = have an operation. 術 is じゅつ, as in 技術.

mnemonic.meaning: The interval (間) between one blink (瞬) and the next. That tiny gap is a moment, an instant.
mnemonic.reading: SHOO! CAN! (しゅんかん) In one instant you shoo the fly and it hits the can.

examples.ja: ドアを開けた瞬間、猫が飛び出した。
examples.en: The moment I opened the door, the cat jumped out.

items.note: 〜た瞬間 = the instant something happened. 一瞬 (いっしゅん) = an instant.

mnemonic.meaning: Everything is in order (順) and in tune (調). The project hums along: it's going smoothly.
mnemonic.reading: JUNE CHOW (じゅんちょう): in June the food arrives on time, the trains run on time. Everything going smoothly.

examples.ja: 新しい仕事は順調に進んでいる。
examples.en: The new job is going smoothly.

items.note: 順調に = smoothly, without trouble.

mnemonic.meaning: You rest (休) and relax (憩) between shifts. That's a break.
mnemonic.reading: On your break you stand in a QUEUE for CAKE (きゅうけい). Best ten minutes of the day.

examples.ja: 二時間働いたら、十分休憩しよう。
examples.en: After two hours of work, let's take a ten-minute break.

items.note: 休憩する = take a short break. 休暇 (きゅうか) = time off, a vacation.

mnemonic.meaning: By chance (偶) it just happened so (然). Neither of you planned it: pure coincidence.
mnemonic.reading: While meditating in ZEN, you step in GOO (ぐうぜん). Total coincidence.

examples.ja: 駅で偶然昔の友達に会った。
examples.en: I ran into an old friend at the station by chance.

items.note: 偶然 = by chance. The opposite is わざと (on purpose).

mnemonic.meaning: You return home (帰) to your house (宅) after a long day. Getting home.
mnemonic.reading: You get home and hang your KEY on a TACK (きたく) by the door.

examples.ja: 毎日、夜八時ごろ帰宅する。
examples.en: I get home around 8 p.m. every day.

items.note: 帰宅 = coming home (a bit formal). 帰国 (きこく) = returning to your country.

mnemonic.meaning: Nothing (無) but worthless (駄) junk in the bag you just bought. What a waste.
mnemonic.reading: A cow watches you buy it and says "MOO... DUH (むだ). That's pointless."

examples.ja: 使わない物を買うのは、お金の無駄だ。
examples.en: Buying things you won't use is a waste of money.

items.note: 無駄 = waste. 無駄にする = to waste something. 無 is む here.

mnemonic.meaning: You transform (化) your face and adorn (粧) it before going out. That's makeup.
mnemonic.reading: Makeup is how KAY gets ready for the SHOW (けしょう).

examples.ja: 姉は出かける前に、三十分も化粧する。
examples.en: My sister spends thirty minutes on makeup before going out.

items.note: 化 is け here (usually か, as in 化学).

mnemonic.meaning: You mix (交) your stuff with a friend's and replace (換) one thing with another. A swap, an exchange.
mnemonic.reading: At the vending machine you trade a COKE for a CAN (こうかん) of tea. Exchange!

examples.ja: サイズが合わなかったので、店で交換してもらった。
examples.en: The size didn't fit, so I had it exchanged at the store.

items.note: 交換 = swap one thing for another. 返品 (へんぴん) = returning something for a refund.

mnemonic.meaning: 飽 has 食 (eat). You eat the same meal so many times you're sick of it. You get tired of it.
mnemonic.reading: "AH, KILL me (あきる), not this show again." You're tired of it.

examples.ja: 同じゲームばかりしていると、すぐ飽きる。
examples.en: If you only play the same game, you soon get bored of it.

items.note: 〜に飽きる = get tired of something. 呆れる (あきれる) = be appalled.

mnemonic.meaning: 叫 has a big 口 (mouth) on the left: a mouth wide open, shouting.
mnemonic.reading: After too much SAKE, you shout "BOO!" (さけぶ) at everyone in the bar.

examples.ja: 火事に気づいた人が「火事だ！」と叫んだ。
examples.en: Someone who noticed the fire shouted, "Fire!"

items.note: 叫ぶ = shout or scream. 呼ぶ (よぶ) = call someone.

mnemonic.meaning: 黙 hides a black (黒) dog (犬). It stares at you, and the whole room goes silent.
mnemonic.reading: Your words hit a DAM, RUE (だまる)... and stop. You go quiet.

examples.ja: 怒られると、弟はいつも黙る。
examples.en: Whenever he gets scolded, my little brother goes quiet.

items.note: 黙る = stop talking. 黙って = without saying anything.

mnemonic.meaning: 揚 means raise: the food rises and bubbles up in the hot oil. Deep-fry, as in 唐揚げ (fried chicken).
mnemonic.reading: 唐揚げ (からあげ) rise in the oil, just like 上げる (あげる, raise). Same sound: deep-fry.

examples.ja: 鶏肉を油で揚げる。
examples.en: I deep-fry the chicken in oil.

items.note: 揚げる = deep-fry (唐揚げ, 天ぷら). Same reading as 上げる (raise).

mnemonic.meaning: 実 is the truth. "As for the truth (実 + は)...": you're about to admit something. Actually...
mnemonic.reading: "GEE, TSUWA... (じつは)" you mumble before confessing. Actually, I forgot. (は reads わ, like the particle.)

examples.ja: 実は、明日の約束を忘れていた。
examples.en: Actually, I'd forgotten about tomorrow's plans.

items.note: 実は = actually, used to admit or reveal something. The は is read わ.

mnemonic.meaning: Your self (自) and your body (身): all of you. Oneself.
mnemonic.reading: I myself (じしん) kept my confidence (自信) through the earthquake (地震): three words, one sound, GEE-SHIN.

examples.ja: これは私自身の問題だから、自分で決める。
examples.en: This is my own problem, so I'll decide for myself.

items.note: 自身 = oneself (私自身 = I myself). 自信 (confidence) and 地震 (earthquake) are also じしん.

mnemonic.meaning: The true (本) person (人): not their lawyer, not their mom. The person themselves.
mnemonic.reading: "HON, NIN-ja (ほんにん) can't sign for you. The person themselves must come."

examples.ja: 手続きには本人が来てください。
examples.en: The person themselves must come in for the procedure.

items.note: 本人 = the person in question, not an agent or a relative.

mnemonic.meaning: You realize (覚) what's coming and reach enlightenment (悟): you accept it. Resolve, being prepared for something hard.
mnemonic.reading: You steel yourself and shout "CACK... GO!" (かくご) and jump. Resolve.

examples.ja: 失敗する覚悟で、挑戦してみた。
examples.en: I gave it a try, prepared to fail.

items.note: 覚悟する = brace yourself for something hard. 覚 is かく here, not おぼ.

mnemonic.meaning: A person (人) you talk about like a thing (物) in a story. A character, a notable person.
mnemonic.reading: The main character drinks GIN and BOOTS (じんぶつ) the villain. What a person!

examples.ja: この小説の中で、一番好きな人物は誰？
examples.en: Who is your favorite character in this novel?

items.note: 人物 = a person, especially a notable one or a character. 物 is ぶつ here, like 動物.

mnemonic.meaning: Monks CHANT TOE-to-toe (ちゃんと), every word properly, neatly, exactly the way it should be.

examples.ja: 朝ご飯はちゃんと食べたほうがいい。
examples.en: You should eat a proper breakfast.

items.note: ちゃんと = properly, as it should be done. ちゃんとした = decent, proper.

mnemonic.meaning: A CANARY (かなり) singing quite loudly: considerably louder than you'd expect from a bird that small.

examples.ja: 今日はかなり寒い。
examples.en: It's quite cold today.

items.note: かなり = quite, more than you might expect. 相当 is similar but a bit stronger.

mnemonic.meaning: TONY CACKLES (とにかく) on and on, so you cut him off: "Anyway, let's go!"

examples.ja: 理由はあとで話すから、とにかく来てください。
examples.en: I'll explain why later, so just come anyway.

items.note: とにかく = anyway: set the details aside and do the main thing first.

mnemonic.meaning: The image (象) stamped (印) on your mind when you first meet someone. An impression.
mnemonic.reading: Your first impression happens IN the SHOW (いんしょう), on stage.

examples.ja: 彼女の第一印象はとてもよかった。
examples.en: My first impression of her was very good.

items.note: 象 is しょう here, with a long vowel. 第一印象 = first impression.

mnemonic.meaning: You record (記) something and later recollect (憶) it. A memory of the past.
mnemonic.reading: You carve a memory into an OAK tree with your KEY (きおく).

examples.ja: 子どものころの記憶は、あまりない。
examples.en: I don't have many memories from my childhood.

items.note: 記憶 = what you remember. 記録 (きろく) = a written record.

mnemonic.meaning: 慌 has 忄 (heart): your heart races and you panic.
mnemonic.reading: "AWW, WHAT A TERRible mess (あわてる), I'm late!" you panic.

examples.ja: 地震が起きても、慌てる必要はない。
examples.en: Even if an earthquake happens, there's no need to panic.

items.note: 慌てて = in a hurry, flustered. The opposite is 落ち着く (to calm down).

mnemonic.meaning: Interest (興) that stirs you up (奮) until you can't sit still. Excitement, getting worked up.
mnemonic.reading: COKE, FUN (こうふん)! Two cans of cola and the kids are bouncing off the walls with excitement.

examples.ja: 試合に勝って、みんな興奮していた。
examples.en: We won the game and everyone was excited.

items.note: 興奮する = get excited or worked up.

mnemonic.meaning: Behind (後) you, after it's too late, comes regret (悔).
mnemonic.reading: You drank the COKE, then CRY (こうかい) because you were on a diet. Regret.

examples.ja: 若いころもっと勉強すればよかったと後悔している。
examples.en: I regret not studying more when I was young.

items.note: 後悔する = regret. 航海 (also こうかい) = a sea voyage.

mnemonic.meaning: Your bag stagnates (滞) in one hotel room while you exist (在) in that city for two weeks. A stay.
mnemonic.reading: On your stay in THAILAND you SIGH (たいざい) happily on the beach every day.

examples.ja: 日本には二週間滞在する予定だ。
examples.en: I plan to stay in Japan for two weeks.

items.note: 滞在 = staying somewhere for a while, e.g. on a trip or at a hotel.
